title: Korean Beef Mince Bowl
summary: A quick, flavourful weeknight dinner, ready in 25 minutes. Sesame oil and ginger give it an authentic Korean flavour.

steps.text: Have the rice cooked and ready.
Put a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the beef mince and break it up with a spatula. Brown until no longer pink, {timer:5-7}. Drain off the excess fat if you prefer.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for {timer:1-2}, until fragrant.
Pour in the soy sauce and sesame oil and add the spring onions. Stir well and simmer for {timer:2-3} to let the flavours meld.
Divide the rice evenly between the bowls, and spoon the beef over. Add vegetables or a fried egg, if you like. Garnish with sesame seeds or extra spring onions.

tips: For vegetables, my favourites here are carrots and peppers, both cut into matchsticks (julienne). Toss them into the pan with the beef for the last 2 minutes if you like them soft, or pile them on raw for crunch. For a tangy Korean flavour, quick-pickle vegetables in rice vinegar, sugar and salt for 10 minutes, or use pickled vegetables.
Rice roughly triples in weight as it cooks, so a third of the cooked weight in raw rice is enough.
As a guide, a garlic clove is about 4 g and a spring onion about 10 g.
